Write the free-text debriefing answers to a private coding file

Source: R/fba-debrief-coding.R
write_debrief_coding.Rd

The free-text answers to the debriefing question asking whether the participant knew or guessed what the study tested must be coded before any blocking index is computed, from a file that holds nothing but participant identifiers and debriefing answers, so that the coding is blind to the test data. write_debrief_coding() writes such a file to the private folder as a CSV with an empty column blocking_naive for the codes indicating whether, based on the debriefing answer, the participant appears to be naive to the study's purpose to investigate blocking. Fill it in manually with TRUE or FALSE, then read the codes back with read_debrief_coding().

Usage

write_debrief_coding(
  debrief,
  file,
  rule = NULL,
  dir = Sys.getenv("CATLAS_PRIVATE_DIR")
)

Arguments

debrief

A data frame with one row per participant and the columns id, prior_knowledge (the yes/no answer) and prior_guess (the free text), taken from the debriefing records of the parsed jsPsych data.

file

Character(1). Path of the coding file (.csv) within the private folder, e.g. "fba-allergy-online-02/debrief-coding.csv".

rule

Character(1) or NULL. The coding rule, printed in the message as a reminder. Defaults to NULL.

dir

Character(1). The private folder. Defaults to the environment variable CATLAS_PRIVATE_DIR, which belongs in .Renviron.

Value

The path of the coding file, invisibly.

Details

Repeated calls

The debriefing file grows with the data. When it exists, codes already entered are kept, participants new to debrief are added with an empty code, and participants absent from debrief keep their rows. A participant whose answer differs from the one in the file aborts the call, as answers cannot change between pulls, so a difference means that participant identifiers no longer match.

Answers that need no coding

A missing answer (for which is.na(prior_guess), e.g. after a timed-out debriefing screen) cannot show that the participant was naive to blocking, so it is coded FALSE automatically and the participant does not reach the naive set (i.e., data set of participants naive to the experimental design).

The file

UTF-8, comma-separated, sorted by id, with empty cells for missing values. Spreadsheet programs may change the separator or translate TRUE and FALSE (e.g. into PRAVDA and NEPRAVDA) when saving; read_debrief_coding() accepts semicolons, but aborts on any code other than TRUE or FALSE.

See also

read_debrief_coding()
